A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chameleon/AIDE study, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. The supplied v2 ends with references; v3 includes Appendices A–E, which are included in this comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 report original AIDE and Chameleon evaluations, perturbation experiments and component ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains original evaluations and adds average-precision results, hyperparameter and backbone experiments, and Grad-CAM analyses in its appendix.

M1.justification: AIDE retains DCT-based patch selection, SRM filtering, two ResNet-50 encoders, OpenCLIP-ConvNeXt semantic features and the same fusion/classification procedure. The appendix tests an alternative backbone as an ablation without changing the proposed method.

E1.justification: AIGCDetectBenchmark, GenImage and Chameleon retain the same generator and category coverage. Additional experiments vary existing corruption severities and model configurations within that coverage.

E2.justification: GramNet is removed from the reported robustness comparison in Table 6, although retained elsewhere. Other existing comparator sets remain unchanged. Newly discussed FatFormer, CLIPMoLE and SSP are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 6 extends JPEG testing from QF 95/90 to include 75/50 and Gaussian blur from sigma 1/2 to include 3/4. Appendix B adds patch-size 16/32/64, patch-count 1/2/3 and backbone comparisons. Main training settings and the stated Acc/AP metrics remain unchanged; Appendix A's sample counts are additional disclosure.

E4.justification: V2's component-removal ablations and qualitative examples are retained. V3 substantially broadens analysis with patch-size/count sensitivity, ConvNeXt-versus-ViT testing, Grad-CAM localization and stronger corruption tests. These examine design choices and feature behavior beyond the original branch-ablation questions.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests or uncertainty bars. Reported means aggregate benchmark performance rather than repeated runs.

E6.justification: Under unchanged stated training settings, Table 5 revises AIDE's Chameleon accuracies from 56.45/61.10/63.89 to 58.37/62.60/65.77 for ProGAN/SD v1.4/all-GenImage training; fake-image scores change while real-image scores remain fixed. V3 adds the AP matrix in Table 12, including mean AP 98.18 for AIDE versus 95.84 for PatchCraft, plus robustness and supplementary-analysis results. Tables 3, 4 and 7 retain their scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same mathematical definitions and operations, apart from punctuation and typesetting edits. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the challenging Chameleon benchmark, hybrid-feature AIDE, stronger public-benchmark performance and unresolved real-world detection difficulty. The headline improvements of 3.5 and 4.6 percentage points remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds explanations for extreme patch sizes and speculates that ConvNeXt benefits from learning more low-level information. Appendix C newly acknowledges limited dataset scale. The central interpretation of Chameleon's difficulty remains unchanged, and the societal-impact discussion is relocated without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Tables 10–11 disclose additional benchmark details, including training counts of 360k ProGAN and 324k SD v1.4 fake images and an equal-real-image convention. Existing implementation settings, hardware, training time, project-page access and EULA requirements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds FatFormer, CLIPMoLE and SSP. The appendix adds baseline summaries and references supporting dataset provenance and Grad-CAM. These extend coverage without substantially changing AIDE's research positioning; publication-year and venue updates identify existing works.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized language corrections and paragraph refinements, updates the conference header, adds acknowledgements and organizes supplementary material into Appendices A–E. The main six-section narrative remains intact, and societal impacts move from the conclusion area to Appendix E.

P2.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes experimental displays: Table 1 is transposed, Tables 4/6/7 are repositioned, and the original Figures 3–4 appear side by side with captions labeled Tables 8–9. New benchmark/AP tables and sensitivity/Grad-CAM figures expand the visual evidence. References to Figures 8–9 conflict with those table captions.

improvement.justification: V3 fills v2's unfulfilled appendix references with experimental details and AP results, while adding useful sensitivity, backbone and localization evidence and a dataset-scale limitation. This improves completeness and support for design choices. The overall gain is limited: the central method and headline benchmark evidence remain unchanged, Table 5's score revisions are unexplained, and figure/table reference mismatches introduce presentation errors.
